item.title: Woodward/Newman Award 2027-28 (Constellation Stage & Screen)
item.description:
Organisation: Constellation Stage & Screen

Location: Bloomington, Indiana, USA. Open submissions of unpublished plays; production takes place in Bloomington.

Award: USD 3,000 cash prize (in lieu of royalties) plus a full production in Constellation's Mainstage season; housing and transportation provided. No submission fee.

Duration: Winner announced by 15 May 2027; production in the 2027-28 season. Submissions stay on file and under consideration for two years.

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

The Woodward/Newman Award, started with the support of Joanne Woodward, Newman's Own Foundation and the Newman family, is awarded annually by Constellation Stage & Screen to the best unpublished new play. The winner receives a USD 3,000 cash prize (in lieu of royalties) and a full production in the Mainstage season, with housing and transportation provided. The contest format and submission fees have been eliminated: submissions are reviewed on an ongoing basis and are also considered for all seven production slots in the season, including TYA (theatre for young audiences) shows. Full-length plays should run 75 to 135 minutes; TYA shows over 40 minutes. Plays must be unpublished at submission (independently published is acceptable); limit of two submissions per playwright per year; musicals may include demos. Plays submitted by midnight 31 August 2026 are considered for the 2027-28 season; later submissions roll to 2028-29. All submissions are kept on file for two years.

Open call details

item.title: XENO Prize for Artists' Books
item.description:
Organisation: Franklin Furnace

Location: United States.

Award: USD 5,000 to one artist to publish one book on the topic of book banning and/or burning, in an edition of at least 100 copies.

Duration: One-time prize

Deadline: Closed 04 Jul 2026

In pursuit of its mission to present, preserve, interpret, educate, and advocate on behalf of avant-garde art, especially forms that may be vulnerable due to institutional neglect, cultural bias, their ephemeral nature, or politically unpopular content, Franklin Furnace offers the annual XENO Prizes for Artists' Books. One artist will receive USD 5,000 to publish one book on the topic of book banning and/or burning in an edition of at least 100 copies. Deadline: July 4, 2026.

item.title: PLAYA Art/Sci Awarded Residency 2027
item.description:
Organisation: PLAYA

Location: Summer Lake, Lake County, Oregon, USA

Award: Awarded residency providing free lodging in a private cabin with kitchen and bathroom plus one weekly group meal. Residents cover their own travel, groceries, and materials. No cash stipend. USD 40 application fee (waivers granted on request by June 28, 2026)

Duration: 11 to 25 nights depending on session

Deadline: Closed 30 Jun 2026

PLAYA's Art/Sci Awarded Residency brings together artists and scientists for immersive, interdisciplinary inquiry at a rural retreat near Summer Lake in Lake County, Oregon. The 2027 cycle offers four session options ranging from 11 to 25 nights between January and November 2027. Awarded residents receive free lodging in a private cabin with kitchen and bathroom plus one weekly group meal, while covering their own travel, food, and materials. Both established and emerging practitioners in any media may apply, including naturalists, biologists, sound artists, new media artists, writers, performers, and interdisciplinary creators, and all applicants must be at least 18 years old. Applications are submitted through SlideRoom and require work samples and two references. There is a USD 40 application fee, though PLAYA states all fee waiver requests will be granted if submitted by June 28, 2026.

Open call details

item.title: Fulbright-Iméra Mediterranean Studies Award 2027-2028 (Aix-Marseille, US Faculty)
item.description:
Organisation: Iméra – Aix Marseille Université, in partnership with the Fulbright Commission

Location: Aix-Marseille, France (campus residency)

Award: €2,400 (~USD 2,600) monthly stipend; fully covered accommodation (valued USD 788–1,966/month); €1,200 (~USD 1,300) travel allowance. No application fee.

Duration: 5 or 10 months (September 2027 – June 2028, flexible start/end dates).

Deadline: 15 Sep 2026

The Fulbright-Iméra Mediterranean Studies Award supports US faculty to conduct research at the Iméra Institute for Advanced Study at Aix Marseille Université. ELIGIBILITY: mid-career, senior, or community college faculty affiliated with a US institution of higher education; US citizens residing outside France (permanent residents of France are ineligible); any discipline relating to Mediterranean studies; English sufficient (French desirable). 1 or 2 grants awarded. PROVIDED: €2,400/month stipend; fully equipped apartment with linens; office in co-working space; visa fees waived; academic event organisation expenses covered; school placement assistance for dependents. DURATION: 5 or 10 months (September 2027 – June 2028, flexible). DEADLINE: 15 September 2026. Apply via the Fulbright Scholar Program at https://fulbrightscholars.org/award/fulbright-imera-mediterranean-studies-award-aix-marseille-university.

Open call details

item.title: BMI Foundation Babyface Award 2026
item.description:
Organisation: BMI Foundation

Location: USA; remote application.

Award: $10,000 career grant plus artistic and business mentorship. No application fee.

Duration: One-time award.

Deadline: Closed 30 Jun 2026

The BMI Foundation Babyface Award is an inaugural annual award supporting emerging songwriters working in R&B, hip-hop, soul, and music of the African diaspora. Founded with a $25,000 investment from Wells Fargo. AMOUNT: $10,000 career grant plus artistic and business mentorship. ELIGIBILITY: ages 18-29 as of 30 June 2026; US residents or those in US territories; submitted works must be unpublished and unassigned to major labels or publishers (self-released works are eligible); co-written works are eligible if all writers meet the eligibility criteria (maximum 3 writers; award split evenly). One application per person per year; cannot submit the same work to multiple BMI Foundation programs. No affiliation with BMI required. APPLICATION MATERIALS: a 1-2 minute personal statement video; two audio files with anonymized lyric sheets (lyrics may be in any language with English translation); and a description of the creative process (audio, visual, or written format). No application fee. Apply via Google Form at https://bmifoundation.org/by-application/babyfaceaward. Deadline: 30 June 2026.

Open call details

item.title: Artadia Awards 2026: San Francisco Bay Area
item.description:
Organisation: Artadia

Location: San Francisco Bay Area, California, United States

Award: Three Awardees each receive a US$15,000 unrestricted award. Finalists not chosen as Awardees receive an honorarium. Awardees also access the Artadia Network and the Online Artist Registry. No application fee.

Duration: One-off award; two-round jury (application review + virtual studio visits)

Deadline: Closed 01 Jun 2026

Artadia's open call for the San Francisco Bay Area, providing unrestricted financial support, exposure and recognition to contemporary visual artists. Three Awardees receive $15,000 each (use freely); Finalists not chosen as Awardees receive an honorarium. Awardees join the Artadia Network and get a dedicated webpage on the Artadia Online Artist Registry. PROCESS: open call (May 1 - June 1, 2026); first-round jury of three curators (one local) selects six Finalists; second-round jury conducts 45-minute virtual studio visits; three Awardees announced. ELIGIBILITY: contemporary visual artist making work for a contemporary-art context; living and working in the Bay Area's eligible counties and resident there for 2+ consecutive years prior to the deadline; not currently enrolled (or planning to enrol) in an art-related degree programme; have never received an Artadia/Art Council award of $10,000 or more (former finalists may re-apply). Apply via Submittable only.

Open call details

item.title: AWS Imagine Grant US 2026: Pathfinder Award (Frontier AI)
item.description:
Organisation: Amazon Web Services (AWS Imagine Grant Program)

Location: United States (registered 501(c) nonprofits only; educational institutions are excluded)

Award: Up to $200,000 USD unrestricted cash + up to $100,000 USD in AWS Promotional Credits + project implementation support from the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center

Duration: Two-round process. Round Two finalists invited to submit a full proposal; results announced mid-November 2026 (public announcement 1 December 2026).

Deadline: Closed 05 Jun 2026

Top-tier track of the 2026 AWS Imagine Grant for US nonprofits with strong data practices, in the planning phase of incorporating frontier AI (generative AI, agentic AI, autonomous systems) as a core workload. Up to $200K cash + $100K AWS credits, plus hands-on project implementation support from the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center, training, and ongoing access. Two-round selection: Round One (open call) closes 5 June 2026; Round Two opens 10 August (invitation-only) and closes 14 September 2026; results mid-November; public announcement 1 December 2026. Eligibility: registered 501(c) nonprofits headquartered in the US. Educational institutions are explicitly excluded. NOTE: this is a nonprofit-only programme and is not open to individual artists, researchers, or for-profit studios.

Open call details
